title: Torsion coefficient assembly
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square],

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{array}
$$

with $f$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $g$ arbitrary, and let $F$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], regarded as a complex concentrated in degree $0$, an object of $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Then the derived exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]

$$
\Ex_{\square,F}:g^{-1}Rf_*F\longrightarrow Rf'_*g'^{-1}F
$$

is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$. Equivalently, for every $p\in\mathbf Z$ the induced map of cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^p(\Ex_{\square,F})$ is an isomorphism; through $\mathcal H^p(g^{-1}Rf_*F)\cong g^{-1}\mathcal H^p(Rf_*F)=g^{-1}R^pf_*F$ and $\mathcal H^p(Rf'_*g'^{-1}F)=R^pf'_*g'^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] this is the base change map $g^{-1}R^pf_*F\to R^pf'_*g'^{-1}F$.

proof.text: Convert IsTorsionAbelianSheaf F to local torsion using Scheme.isTorsionAbelianSheaf_characterizations. The equivalence Phi from sheaves of ULift Z-modules to abelian sheaves (AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.isEquivalence_sheafCompose_forget₂_uliftInt) supplies its canonical inverse image F' and counit e : Phi(F') ≅ F. Scheme.isTorsionSheaf_iff_isTorsion, Scheme.IsTorsionSheaf.of_iso and Scheme.isTorsionModuleSheaf_iff_isTorsion show that F' is torsion. This is transport along a proved equivalence, with no arbitrary witness of an unproved existence theorem.

proof.text: Put K' = F'[0]. DerivedCategory.Plus.moduleTorsionHomology_singleFunctor_obj supplies torsion cohomology. Apply hasTorsionBaseChange_of_isProper (ULift Z) f sq K'. This is the declaration attached to lemma-weil-pbc-prime-proper-base-change; its current signature already covers arbitrary module coefficients and torsion cohomology. Its proof retains the unit route: the projective-line computation and reduction, followed by hasTorsionBaseChange_of_forall_prime and the prime-factor/filtered-colimit devissage. Thus the nine-step planned assembly is reused from the library rather than repeated here.

proof.text: The exact functor Phi gives eK : Phi_derived(K') ≅ F[0] by mapDerivedCategoryPlusSingleFunctor and singleFunctor.mapIso e. NatTrans.isIso_app_iff_of_iso transfers the component along eK, and isIso_derivedBaseChangeMapPlus_app_forget₂_iff transfers the specified derived exchange between module and abelian coefficients. The already proved DerivedForget compatibility identifies these actual exchange maps, not just their endpoints. This yields the first conjunct. Every homology functor preserves isomorphisms, yielding all degrees and the second conjunct.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ and every proper Cartesian square, the
specific map $\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,F}$ is an isomorphism.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Write $F=\varinjlim_nF[n]$ and commute both sides of exchange with the
filtered colimit. Induct on the number of prime factors of $n$ through
$0\to F[\ell]\to F[n]\to F[n]/F[\ell]\to0$; the quotient is killed by
$n/\ell$. Prime coefficients are handled by the preceding lemma, and the
five-lemma transfer handles the induction step. Naturality shows at every
stage that the comparison is the S0 exchange map.

blueprint_notes.label: status
blueprint_notes.text:
**Status.** The route above reaches the statement for every proper $f$:
neither [lemma-weil-pbc-prime-proper-base-change] nor the reduction
[prop-weil-pbc-reduction-to-projective-line] carries a finite-presentation
hypothesis, since the Chow lemma [lemma-weil-pbc-chow-factorization] used in
the reduction is proved for every proper morphism over an affine base. For the
general proper morphism the classical statement is Etale Cohomology,
Theorem 59.91.11 (Tag [095T](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/095T)):
"Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes. Let $g:Y'\to Y$ be a morphism
of schemes ... Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian torsion sheaf on
$X_{\acute{e}tale}$. Then the base change map $g^{-1}Rf_*\mathcal{F}\to
Rf'_*(g')^{-1}\mathcal{F}$ is an isomorphism." Its proof follows the same
route as the one above: the reduction to $\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ for every
scheme $S$ is Etale Cohomology, Lemma 59.91.10 (Tag
[0A4F](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A4F)), and the strictly henselian
computation is the comparison $\Gamma(X,\mathcal{F})=\Gamma(Z,\mathcal{F}|_Z)$
of Lemma 59.91.1 (Tag [0A0B](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A0B)), which
Stacks derives from Stein factorization (More on Morphisms, Theorem 37.53.5,
Tag [03H2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03H2)) and henselian
idempotent lifting (More on Algebra, Lemma 15.11.8, Tag
[09XK](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09XK)). Accordingly the only
inputs of this route that the chapter does not supply are the two Stein
inputs [thm-weil-pbc-stein-inputs]; they are supplied in the literature by
the chain just named, and closing them here means decomposing that chain.

blueprint_update.statement:
For every proper $f:X\to Y$, every cartesian base change, and every torsion
abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$, the derived exchange morphism
$\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,F}$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] is an
isomorphism in every cohomological degree. This is the sheaf-level instance,
for $K=F[0]$, of the bounded-below proper base change theorem of this
chapter, whose exchange isomorphism has these degreewise maps as its
cohomology-sheaf components.

proof.text:
If $nF=0$ and $n=rn'$, the prime-factor devissage sequence expresses $F$
through an $\mathbf F_r$-module sheaf and a sheaf killed by $n'$; the long
exact direct-image sequences, the prime-coefficient case
[lemma-weil-pbc-prime-proper-base-change], and the five-lemma transfer induct on the
number of prime factors of $n$. For arbitrary torsion $F$, the filtered union
of its finite-order subsheaves and the exact filtered-colimit theorem for
direct images pass the isomorphism to the colimit; naturality keeps the
comparison equal to the named exchange morphism of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange].
